classification.habit: Erect perennial rhizomatous herb, 10–60 cm, alpine Himalaya 3000–5000 m
classification.habitat: Moist alpine slopes, rocky grassland and meadows of the Himalaya at about 3000–5000 m.
classification.distribution: Alpine Himalaya of Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh; a threatened, CITES-listed species.

identification.description: Dark brown highly fibrous woody rhizomes crowned with dense reddish-brown tufts of fibrous leaf-remnants, intensely aromatic heavy musky-earthy odor, bitter acrid taste.
identification.whole_plant: Small erect perennial herb 10–60 cm high arising from a stout woody rhizome covered with fibrous remains of old leaf bases.
identification.root: Dried rhizome dark brown, 2.5–7.5 cm long, cylindrical, covered with reddish-brown fibres forming a network (skeletons of sheathing leaf bases); fracture brittle, inside reddish-brown; strongly aromatic, taste acrid and slightly bitter.
identification.stem: Aerial flowering stem erect, slender, more or less hairy, bearing one or two pairs of sessile leaves.
identification.leaf: Radical leaves long, spathulate to oblong-lanceolate with parallel longitudinal veins; stem leaves few, opposite, sessile.
identification.flower: Small pale pink to purplish flowers in dense terminal cymose heads; corolla campanulate, five-lobed, with four stamens.
identification.fruit: Small obovoid one-seeded fruit, covered with hairs and crowned by persistent calyx teeth.
identification_points: Dark brown highly fibrous woody rhizomes crowned with dense reddish-brown tufts of fibrous leaf-remnants, intensely aromatic heavy musky-earthy odor, bitter acrid taste.

therapeutics.dose: Churna 2–3 g; decoction 5–10 g of drug (API)
therapeutics.precautions: Sedative action may add to other CNS depressants. The species is threatened; use authenticated, legally sourced rhizome and do not confuse it with Tagara (Valeriana jatamansi).
therapeutics.contraindications: Avoid with sedative or hypnotic drugs without supervision; avoid unsupervised use in pregnancy and lactation owing to limited safety data.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The rhizome contains an essential oil rich in sesquiterpenes such as jatamansone (valeranone), together with coumarins and resinous matter.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Calms the mind, supports mental clarity, and acts as a nervine tonic.
recognized_uses: Studied for sedative, anticonvulsant and antioxidant activity in experimental models
modern_information.safety_notes: Generally tolerated in pharmacopoeial doses; may cause drowsiness. Wild-harvested supplies are under conservation pressure and adulteration is common.

exam_points: Botanical name: Nardostachys jatamansi; Family: Caprifoliaceae (Valerianaceae)
Rasa: Tikta-Kashaya-Madhura; Guna: Laghu-Snigdha; Virya: Sheeta; Vipaka: Katu
Key karma: Medhya, Nidrajanana, Manasadoshahara, Keshya
Key constituent: jatamansone (valeranone) in the essential oil
viva_questions: What is the botanical source and family of Jatamansi?
Describe the macroscopy of the Jatamansi rhizome.
How is Jatamansi differentiated from Tagara?

student.quick_revision: Jatamansi (Nardostachys jatamansi): rhizome; Tikta-Kashaya-Madhura rasa, Laghu-Snigdha guna, Sheeta virya, Katu vipaka; Tridoshashamaka, mainly Kapha-Pitta; Medhya, Nidrajanana; key in Unmada, Apasmara, Anidra.

teaching_points: Use the fibrous "jata" (hair-like) covering to explain the name Jatamansi.
Contrast Jatamansi with Tagara (Valeriana jatamansi) as Medhya-Nidrajanana drugs.
Discuss conservation status and sustainable sourcing of alpine drugs.
discussion_points: Medhya and Nidrajanana actions of Jatamansi
Conservation status of Nardostachys jatamansi and use of cultivated material
practical_points: Examine the rhizome for the fibrous network and odour.
Compare authentic rhizome with Tagara samples.

doctor.quick_reference: Jatamansi is a Sheeta, Medhya and Nidrajanana rhizome used in Anidra, Unmada, Apasmara and Manasaroga; churna 2–3 g (API).
doctor.dose: Churna 2–3 g; decoction 5–10 g of drug (API)
